{{Short description|Italian-British mathematician}}
'''Valerio Lucarini''' (born 11 August 1976 in Ancona, Italy<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Ilire Hasani, Robert Hoffmann |title=Academy of Europe: Mathematics and Planet Earth |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/Members_in_Spotlight/Mathematics%20and%20Planet%20Earth |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>) is an Italian and British mathematician, physicist, and climate scientist. He has given key contributions in the area of mathematics and physics of [[climate]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=PR859447 - University of Reading |url=https://www.reading.ac.uk/news/2021/university-news/staff/pr859447 |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=www.reading.ac.uk}}</ref> In particular, he has shown how the use of [[statistical mechanics]] can advance the understanding of the link between forced and free variability of the climate system across multiple scales of motion, define a robust framework for understanding climatic [[Tipping points in the climate system|tipping points]], and improve our ability to interpret and model [[Extreme event attribution|extreme events]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Valerio Lucarini |url=https://www.egu.eu/awards-medals/lewis-fry-richardson/2020/valerio-lucarini/ |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=European Geosciences Union (EGU) |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Kuglitsch |first=Dr Franz G. |title=CMG |url=https://iugg.org/associations-commissions/commissions/cmg/ |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=IUGG |language=de}}</ref> 

He is currently a Professor of Applied Mathematics at the School of Computing and Mathematical Sciences of the [[University of Leicester]], where he coordinates the research group in computational modelling for sciences and engineering.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Valerio Lucarini |url=https://le.ac.uk/people/valerio-lucarini |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=University of Leicester |language=en}}</ref> 

== Honours and awards ==
* 2025 [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?y=2025&af=true|title=Fellows nominated in 2025|work=APS Fellows archive|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=2025-12-14}}</ref>
* 2024 Keilis-Borok Medal, International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics<ref name=":2" />
* 2022 Member, [[Academia Europaea]]<ref name=":0" />
* 2022 Mathematics of Planet Earth Career Prize, Society of Industrial and Applied Mathematics<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prize History {{!}} SIAM Activity Group on Mathematics of Planet Earth Prize {{!}} SIAM |url=https://www.siam.org/programs-initiatives/prizes-awards/activity-group-prizes/siam-activity-group-on-mathematics-of-planet-earth-prize/prize-history/ |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2021 Lorenz Lecture, [[American Geophysical Union]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Myles |first=Susan Lozier, LaToya |date=2021-09-10 |title=2021 AGU Section Awardees and Named Lecturers |url=https://eos.org/agu-news/2021-agu-section-awardees-and-named-lecturers |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=Eos |language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2020 [[Lewis Fry Richardson#Legacy|L.F. Richardson Medal]], European Geophysical Union<ref name=":1" />
* 2018 [[Whitehead Prize]], [[London Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 LMS Prize Winners {{!}} London Mathematical Society |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/29062018-1745/2018-lms-prize-winners |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The European Physical Journal A (EPJ A) |url=https://epja.epj.org/epjplus-news/1522-epjplus-editor-valerio-lucarini-wins-whitehead-prize?mb=0 |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=epja.epj.org}}</ref>
* 2010 Outstanding Young Scientist (now Arne Richter) Award, European Geophysical Union<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arne Richter Awards for Outstanding Early Career Scientists |url=https://www.egu.eu/awards-medals/arne-richter/ |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=European Geosciences Union (EGU) |language=en}}</ref>
